title: Load transient: 1mA <-> 50mA step response
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Load transient" row (1<->50 mA step, ~1us edges: peak excursion <=150mV, recover to +-1% in <=20us, over the ratified C_out/ESR window) against the LDO core-regulation-loop schematic landed by #14 (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch). Both the spec row and the C_out/ESR window (spec/decision-records/DR-002) are ratified by issue #1 / DR-006, and the bounds below cite those numbers verbatim, not an invented final limit. This testbench's undershoot/overshoot measurements are computed as the deviation from the pre-step (light-load) steady-state value, not an absolute vout bound. Issue #180 brought this bench into conformance with sim/README.md's "Initial-condition contract (issue #171)": the transient is released from an eleven-node `.ic`-constrained operating point (#164's variant-B shape, PR #170 -- see testbench/tb_load_transient.sch's header and this manifest's deck.analyses comments) instead of from ngspice's own unconstrained loop-closed `.op`, which 23 of the 45 corner logs in the superseded 20260825-081255-4cb27f8 record show hitting a singular-matrix / gmin-stepping diagnostic. The stimulus, the step timestamps and every ratified bound are unchanged by that conversion; the pre-step reference moved from v(vout)[0] to a 0.800-0.999ms average and the peak searches were windowed to the stepped region, because under an `.ic` seed t=0 is the seed itself rather than the corner's own settled 1mA point. The row has TWO independent clauses and, until #119, this manifest measured only the first: undershoot_v/overshoot_v cover "peak excursion <=150mV", and recovery_rise_us/recovery_fall_us (added in #119) cover "recover to +-1% in <=20us" on the rising and falling load edges respectively. Both clause bounds are quoted verbatim from the same ratified row. Issue #119 also moved C_out from the superseded record's 1uF (DR-002's recommended nominal) to 4.7uF (DR-002's ratified window's own ceiling, still 0-500mOhm ESR -- not a value outside the ratified window) to address the peak-excursion clause, which #119 root-caused as charge-limited (Q=C*dV against the loop's finite large-signal response time, not phase-margin-limited -- see design/README.md's #115 anti-correlation finding). Issue #313 (Phase A) replaced that single point with the finite `window_grid` declared below: C_out in {0.33uF, 4.7uF} x ESR in {0, 10mOhm, 500mOhm} (six legs, including the 4.7uF/10mOhm reference), each leg independently reset and seeded, and every leg measured separately for the rising (1mA->50mA) and falling (50mA->1mA) load edge. This SAMPLES DR-002's window at its corners and its reference point; it is not a continuous proof over the window -- a passing grid cannot rule out an interior worst case. A record is a window-grid campaign only when it carries a `window_grid` block; records minted before #313 measured the single 4.7uF/10mOhm point only, and Phase A mints no full-grid x PVT campaign. See spec/decision-records/DR-002's append and design/README.md's "#119" section for the full per-corner evidence, including the recovery-time clause's own, opposite-direction relationship to C_out (this record's own #119 writeup) that this C_out choice does not close. Known-immature-design caveat (design/README.md "Known gaps"): C_COMP/C_CL remain unsized placeholders and the error amplifier still has a light-load/high-VIN output-swing ceiling (design/README.md's "Known open item") even though issue #22 already added the current-limit and soft-start protection circuitry, so a FAIL here -- especially at the high-VIN corner -- is an honest, expected finding at this design stage (per CLAUDE.md's "Verification is the product"), not a harness defect.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

analyses: * --- initial-condition contract (issue #171), applied by issue #180 ---
* This `tran` deliberately carries NO `uic`: the transient is released from
* an operating-point solve that testbench/tb_load_transient.sch's IC_SEED
* `.ic` card constrains to the loop's intended regulating branch at the
* pre-step 1 mA load. That is #164's variant-B shape (PR #170), the second of
* the two shapes sim/README.md's "Initial-condition contract (issue #171)"
* accepts, and the shape sim/ic-screen-125c-b uses. It was chosen over `uic`
* + an EN-edge preamble because this bench steps the LOAD at an already-
* regulating condition: an EN preamble would shift every timestamp below AND
* make C_OUT's pre-step charge state depend on the soft-start ramp, which
* #119's charge-limited peak-excursion finding (see this manifest's claim)
* requires be held fixed. The step edges (1.000ms / 2.001ms) and the 3ms span
* are therefore unchanged from the superseded 20260825-081255-4cb27f8 record.
* --- window grid (issue #313) ---
* The tran and every .meas/let for this bench live in `window_grid.leg_analyses`,
* which corner-run.py instantiates once per declared COUT/ESR leg (reset, alter,
* tran, measure -- see window_grid.reset_policy). Reference levels, windows and
* the outband/w_rise/w_fall recovery vectors are the #180/#119 definitions, now
* evaluated per leg; the rise/fall peak windows split the old joint 1.000m-2.999m
* search at the fall edge (2.001m) so each step direction is its own result.

measurements.name: undershoot_rise_v
measurements.note: Worst-case dip below the pre-step (light-load, ~1mA) steady-state value on the rise load edge (window t=1.000m..2.001m, the 1mA->50mA edge and its 50mA plateau). Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Load transient" row, peak excursion <=150mV (unchanged). Measured per COUT/ESR leg (issue #313); the pre-#313 undershoot_v/overshoot_v took one joint 1.000m-2.999m window at the single 4.7uF/10mOhm point.

measurements.name: overshoot_rise_v
measurements.note: Worst-case rise above the pre-step steady-state value on the rise load edge (window t=1.000m..2.001m, the 1mA->50mA edge and its 50mA plateau). Same ratified 150mV bound, unchanged; measured per COUT/ESR leg (issue #313).

measurements.name: undershoot_fall_v
measurements.note: Worst-case dip below the pre-step (light-load, ~1mA) steady-state value on the fall load edge (window t=2.001m..2.999m, the 50mA->1mA edge and its recovery). Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Load transient" row, peak excursion <=150mV (unchanged). Measured per COUT/ESR leg (issue #313); the pre-#313 undershoot_v/overshoot_v took one joint 1.000m-2.999m window at the single 4.7uF/10mOhm point.

measurements.name: overshoot_fall_v
measurements.note: Worst-case rise above the pre-step steady-state value on the fall load edge (window t=2.001m..2.999m, the 50mA->1mA edge and its recovery). Same ratified 150mV bound, unchanged; measured per COUT/ESR leg (issue #313).

measurements.name: recovery_rise_us
measurements.note: Recovery time on the 1mA->50mA edge: microseconds from the start of the rising load edge (t=1.000ms) until v(vout) is back inside +-1% of the pre-step value and stays there. Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Load transient" row, "recover to +-1% in <=20us" (ratified by issue #1 / DR-006). Added in #119 -- the row has always had two clauses and until now the harness measured only the peak-excursion one. Read with settle_err_50ma_pct: if that diagnostic is itself outside +-1%, this corner's rising-edge recovery is bounded by steady-state load regulation (the sim/load-regulation row, #118), not by transient settling. Measured per COUT/ESR leg (issue #313); the 20us bound is unchanged.

measurements.name: recovery_fall_us
measurements.note: Recovery time on the 50mA->1mA edge: microseconds from the start of the falling load edge (t=2.001ms, i.e. TD+TR+PW of the PULSE source) until v(vout) is back inside +-1% of the pre-step value and stays there. Same ratified 20us bound as recovery_rise_us. This edge is the harder one by construction: the pass device can only source current, so the excess charge the overshoot leaves on C_out can only be removed by the light load itself, which floors this measurement at C_out*(overshoot_v - 0.01*vout)/I_light regardless of the loop. Measured per COUT/ESR leg (issue #313); the 20us bound is unchanged.

measurements.name: settle_err_50ma_pct
measurements.note: DIAGNOSTIC, no bound -- not a spec claim. Steady-state output error at 50mA (sampled 1ms after the rising edge, just before the falling edge) relative to the pre-step 1mA value (v_pre, the 0.800m-0.999m average), in percent. Present so recovery_rise_us can be read unambiguously: a corner whose 50mA steady state is already outside the +-1% band can never clear recovery_rise_us no matter how fast the loop settles, and that is a DC load-regulation shortfall (sim/load-regulation, #118) surfacing here rather than a transient one. Measured per COUT/ESR leg (issue #313).

window_grid.title: Finite COUT/ESR qualification grid (issue #313, Phase A)
window_grid.justification: spec/decision-records/DR-002 ratifies the window 0.33-4.7 uF with 0-500 mOhm ESR and NO minimum ESR. The grid is the cross product of both COUT endpoints and the three ESR points {0 (the no-minimum-ESR boundary), 10 mOhm (the existing ceramic-representative reference ESR), 500 mOhm (the window's ESR ceiling)}. That puts all four window corners and the pre-existing 4.7 uF / 10 mOhm reference point (#119) in the product. Rationale for endpoints first: peak excursion is charge-limited (Q = C*dV, #119) and so worst at the SMALL-C end, while the falling-edge recovery floor C*(overshoot - 1%)/I_light is worst at the LARGE-C end -- opposite directions in C -- and ESR adds an I*ESR step plus a loop zero, so the extremes of both axes are where a monotone trend would put the worst case. Every measurement is taken separately for the rising and falling load edge.
window_grid.sampling_statement: This is a finite grid that SAMPLES the DR-002 window. It is NOT a continuous-window proof: endpoint and reference legs cannot rule out an interior worst case (e.g. an ESR-zero / loop-crossover interaction at an intermediate C and ESR). If the observed worst cases sit away from the grid corners, the grid must be refined with interior points before any window-qualification claim.
window_grid.zero_esr_topology: ESR = 0 is realised with C_out wired directly from VOUT to ground (the testbench's CDIR branch, no series element), with the series COUT+RESR branch set to 0 F (an open circuit, so RESR carries no current; it is parked at its 10 mOhm netlist value). No nonzero stand-in resistor replaces the boundary. In every ESR > 0 leg CDIR is 0 F and the series branch carries the full COUT.
window_grid.reset_policy: Each leg begins with `reset` (re-parses the circuit, discarding the previous leg's state), re-issues `save all` (reset drops it, leaving only the netlist's `.save` cards), then re-applies ALL of its own `alter` cards, then runs its own `tran`, which re-solves the `.ic`-seeded operating point from the testbench's IC_SEED card (#171/#180 contract). No leg inherits charge, solver state or parameter values from another.
leg_analyses: meas tran v_pre AVG v(vout) FROM=0.800m TO=0.999m
meas tran v_rise_min MIN v(vout) FROM=1.000m TO=2.001m
meas tran v_rise_max MAX v(vout) FROM=1.000m TO=2.001m
meas tran v_fall_min MIN v(vout) FROM=2.001m TO=2.999m
meas tran v_fall_max MAX v(vout) FROM=2.001m TO=2.999m
meas tran v_50ma FIND v(vout) AT=2.000m
